title: Blush Framework admin theme manifest
description: An admin theme's admin-theme.json: its name, label, and description. What it changes is in tokens.json beside it.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema editors check this file with.

schemaVersion.description: The version of the schema this file is written to. Without it, it's 1. Blush reads older versions and refuses newer ones; this schema is version 1.

name.description: The admin theme's name, the key it's known by: vendor/name, such as "acme/gallery". Its folder is extensions/{vendor}/{name}, so it must match the folder. Without it, the name in the composer.json beside this file is used; for a Composer package, it's the package name.

label.description: The admin theme's title, as people read it. Without one, it's shown by its name.

description.description: What the theme looks like, in a few words, shown beside its swatch.

require.description: What the theme needs, as composer.json says it, with version constraints: blush-dev/framework for Blush, and other extensions by vendor/name. A theme whose requirements aren't met isn't offered. Without it, the require in the composer.json beside this file is used.

conflict.description: What the theme can't be offered with, as composer.json says it, each with the versions it can't. Without it, the conflict in the composer.json beside this file is used.

replace.description: The packages the theme stands in for, as composer.json says it. Without it, the replace in the composer.json beside this file is used.

provide.description: The packages the theme provides an implementation of, as composer.json says it. Without it, the provide in the composer.json beside this file is used.

authors.description: Who made the admin theme, as composer.json lists authors. Without it, the authors in the composer.json beside this file are used.

role.description: What they did, such as "Developer" or "Designer".

license.description: How the admin theme may be used: an SPDX identifier such as "MIT", a list of them any of which applies, "(MIT or Apache-2.0)", "(MIT and OFL-1.1)" when all apply, or "proprietary". Common open source licenses link to their text in the admin. Without it, the license in the composer.json beside this file is used.

homepage.description: The admin theme's website. Without it, the homepage in the composer.json beside this file is used.

support.description: Where to get help with the admin theme, as composer.json has it. Without it, the support in the composer.json beside this file is used.

source.description: Where to browse or download the source.

irc.description: An IRC channel, such as irc://irc.libera.chat/example.

security.description: How to report a security issue.

funding.description: Where to fund the admin theme, as composer.json has it. Without it, the funding in the composer.json beside this file is used.

type.description: The kind of funding, such as github, patreon, opencollective, tidelift, ko-fi, or custom.

abandoned.description: Whether the admin theme is no longer maintained: true, or the name of the package to use instead (vendor/name), as composer.json has it. It only warns. Without it, the abandoned in the composer.json beside this file is used.

suggest.description: Packages that would work well with the admin theme, each mapped to why, as composer.json has it: other plugins, themes, or icon packs by vendor/name, libraries, or ext-{name} for PHP extensions. It's only shown, never enforced. Without it, the suggest in the composer.json beside this file is used.

keywords.description: Words the admin theme is about, as composer.json has them. They aren't shown; the admin's lists search them. Without it, the keywords in the composer.json beside this file are used.
